edbDesc: A solution that contains more of the dissolved material than could be dissolved by the solvent under normal circumstances. It can also refer to a vapour of a compound that has a higher (partial) pressure than the vapour pressure of that compound.
title: Supersaturation
description: A hot liquid can dissolve extra salt or sugar and keep it dissolved as it cools, until a speck or a jolt makes it all crystallise at once. Lowitz studied these overloaded solutions and seeding them with a crystal in the 1790s; the same trick makes clickable hand warmers and, in air, the cloud trails of the cloud chamber.
effect: a liquid holds more dissolved than it should until a seed sets it off
usedIn: Cloud chambers for seeing particle tracks
strength: Clicking the metal disc in a hand warmer crystallises the whole pack in seconds and warms it to about 54 degrees.
pickWhy: Specific effect with clear jobs; Lowitz is the usual credit for discovering supersaturated solutions, mid-1790s.
